newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics sees Q2 revs above $899 million.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics sees Q2 revs above $899 million.

text.p: Silicon Graphics Inc Chief Financial Officer Stanley Meresman said the computer company expects second quarter revenues to be slightly higher than year ago levels when Cray Research, now a subsidiary, had a steep spike in revenue.

"The number a year ago was $899 million," he told Reuters in an interview. "We expect to be slightly up from that number a year ago, although that's substantially up from the quarter that just ended in September."
Meresman said SGI expects to be on track for "significant growth" in revenue year-on-year in its fiscal second half.

Meresman declined to forecast specific revenue figures or to comment on analysts' earnings estimates. Wall Street expects the company to post a profit of $1.27 a share for the full fiscal year to June 1997.

"You have to remember that for Cray a year ago December was their fiscal year end, which was a very, very strong quarter, so now when we compare our combined company this year to last year we're comparing to a combined spike in Cray revenue last year that makes the year-to-year comparison tough," he said, adding that Cray's results are expected to be more linear in the current quarter without year-end pressure.
Silicon Graphics posted first quarter revenue for its first fiscal quarter of $766 million, just above its prior-year figure of $758 million.

"We certainly are ramping up this quarter in our production and in the second half of our fiscal year which ends in June we would expect that to be on track for significant growth year over year for the second half of the year," he said.
